title: Scalar-extension maps form morphisms of distinguished triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of its module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Write $D(R)$ and $D(S)$ for the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of their abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $Q_R,Q_S$ for localization from homotopy categories. Let $F=-\otimes_R^LS:D(R)\to D(S)$ be the exact derived scalar-extension functor computed by K-flat resolutions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Let $U:D(S)\to D(R)$ be termwise restriction of scalars along $\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; use its exact derived functor, computed termwise, with the unchanged underlying abelian sheaves [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Give these functors their canonical shift structures from the complexes, using $(P[1])^i=P^{i+1}$ and $d_{P[1]}=-d_P$ [def-weil-triangulated-category].

There is a canonical natural transformation $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{D(R)}\to UF$ with the following characterization. For every complex $C$ and every K-flat resolution $p:P\to C$, under the canonical identification $F(Q_RC)\cong Q_S(P\otimes_R S)$, its component is represented by the roof
$$Q_RC\xleftarrow{\ Q_Rp\ }Q_RP\xrightarrow{\ Q_R i_P\ }UQ_S(P\otimes_R S),\qquad i_P(x)=x\otimes1.$$
This characterization is independent of the resolution. If $\chi_X:UF(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(UF X)[1]$ is the composite canonical shift comparison, then
$$\chi_X\circ\eta_{X[1]}=\eta_X[1]$$
for every $X\in D(R)$. For every distinguished triangle $\Delta=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$, the three components $(\eta_X,\eta_Y,\eta_Z)$ give a morphism of distinguished triangles $\Delta\to UF(\Delta)$, with connecting square
$$\chi_X\circ UF(w)\circ\eta_Z=\eta_X[1]\circ w.$$
No flatness of $S$ over $R$, boundedness, constructibility, or existence of points of the site is assumed.

proof.text: Let $E(P)=P\otimes_R S$ on complexes and let $V$ be termwise restriction of scalars. The map $i_P:P\to VE(P)$ is defined by the sectionwise map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ followed by sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. It is $R$-linear and commutes with restriction maps and differentials: $d(x\otimes1)=d(x)\otimes1$. For a chain map $a:P\to P'$ one has $VE(a)i_P=i_{P'}a$. For a chain homotopy $h$ the termwise tensor homotopy is $h\otimes1$, since $E(dh+hd)=E(d)E(h)+E(h)E(d)$. Thus $E,V$ and $i$ are defined on the homotopy categories. Restriction leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged, so preserves kernels and sheafified cokernels [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. It is exact; [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives $U$ and the termwise identification $UQ_S\cong Q_RV$, compatible with the canonical shifts.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal P$ for the full homotopy subcategory of K-flat $R$-complexes with flat terms, $W$ for its quasi-isomorphisms and $L=Q_R|_{\mathcal P}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $W^{-1}\mathcal P\to D(R)$ is an equivalence; consequently $L$ is a localization at $W$ (compose its localization equivalence with that equivalence). By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $Q_SE$ inverts $W$, and on $\mathcal P$ there is the canonical comparison $c_P:F(LP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_SE(P)$. This comparison is natural: it is the restriction of the derived-functor counit, whose naturality and invertibility on the resolving class are stated in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Compose with the termwise restriction identification of Step 1 to obtain $b_P:UF(LP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_RVE(P)$. Define $j_P=b_P^{-1}Q_R(i_P):LP\to UF(LP)$. Step 1 and naturality of $b$ make $j$ a natural transformation $L\to UF\circ L$. Both functors invert $W$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], applied to this $L$, extends $j$ uniquely to $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{D(R)}\to UF$.

proof.text: First suppose $p:P\to C$ is a K-flat resolution with flat terms. Naturality of $\eta$ for $Q_Rp$ gives $\eta_{Q_RC}=UF(Q_Rp)\eta_{Q_RP}(Q_Rp)^{-1}$. The resolution identification is $F(Q_RC)\xrightarrow{F(Q_Rp)^{-1}}F(Q_RP)\xrightarrow{c_P}Q_SE(P)$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. In that identification the last equality becomes exactly $Q_R(i_P)(Q_Rp)^{-1}$, the required roof. This also proves uniqueness from the roof characterization: every complex has such a resolution by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and every object of $D(R)$ is represented by a complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YY, resolution comparison; agent calculation of the component

proof.text:
Now let $p:P\to C$ be any K-flat resolution, with no condition on its terms. Choose a K-flat resolution $t:T\to P$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Then $pt:T\to C$ is another such resolution. Put $a=Q_Rt$ and $e=UQ_S(E(t))$. Both are isomorphisms: for $e$ use clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], since both $T$ and $P$ are K-flat. The sectionwise equality $E(t)i_T=i_Pt$ gives $eQ_R(i_T)=Q_R(i_P)a$. Multiplying by $a^{-1}(Q_Rp)^{-1}$ gives
$$eQ_R(i_T)(Q_R(pt))^{-1}=Q_R(i_P)(Q_Rp)^{-1}.$$
The canonical comparison between the $T$ and $P$ computations of $F(Q_RC)$ is $Q_SE(t)$ by naturality of its derived counit [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Hence the already established roof for $pt$ is the proposed roof for $p$. Every roof therefore represents the same $\eta_{Q_RC}$, proving independence of all resolutions, not merely those with flat terms.

proof.text: The class $\mathcal P$ is stable under $[1]$: terms are merely reindexed, and the total tensor with $P[1]$ is the shift of the total tensor with $P$ (in a term $A^a\otimes P^{b+1}$ the comparison multiplies by $(-1)^a$); thus the K-flat test remains acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex]. On scalar extension, $S$ is in degree zero and the termwise comparison $\theta_P:E(P[1])\to E(P)[1]$ is the identity, since both differentials are $-d_P\otimes1$. Restriction likewise has identity termwise shift comparison $\tau$, and $\varphi$ of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] is compatible with it (its clause (2)). Therefore $i_{P[1]}=i_P[1]$ degree by degree: both send $x\in P^{r+1}$ to $x\otimes1$. The canonical shift structure $\sigma$ of $F$ is the unique one for which the derived counit $\varepsilon$ commutes with $\theta$ and the shift isomorphisms of $Q_R,Q_S$ [lem-sbc-derived-scalar-extension-counit-shift]; $c_P=\varepsilon_P$ on $\mathcal P$. For $P\in\mathcal P$, naturality of $\eta$ at $s_P:Q_R(P[1])\cong(Q_RP)[1]$ gives $\eta_{(Q_RP)[1]}=UF(s_P)\,j_{P[1]}\,s_P^{-1}$. Insert the definitions $j=b^{-1}Q_R(i)$ at $P$ and $P[1]$; the two compatibilities just cited turn $\chi_{Q_RP}\eta_{(Q_RP)[1]}$ into $b_P[1]^{-1}\,Q_R(i_P)[1]$, which is $\eta_{Q_RP}[1]$. Thus the two natural transformations $\chi\circ\eta_{[1]}$ and $\eta[1]$ from $[1]$ to $[1]\circ UF$ agree at every $L(P)$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] then makes them equal on $D(R)$. This proves $\chi_X\eta_{X[1]}=\eta_X[1]$ with the specified sign convention.

source.place: Tag 06YY, canonical shift structure of the K-flat derived functor; agent calculation using the tensor differential and derived.tex Definition 014V

proof.text:
Let $\Delta=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$ be distinguished. The functor $F$ with its canonical shift structure $\sigma$ is triangulated by [lem-sbc-derived-scalar-extension-counit-shift], and $U$ with its termwise shift structure is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] clause (1) (the functor of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]). Thus $UF(\Delta)$ is distinguished and has last arrow $\chi_XUF(w)$. Naturality gives $UF(u)\eta_X=\eta_Yu$ and $UF(v)\eta_Y=\eta_Zv$, and at $w$ it gives $UF(w)\eta_Z=\eta_{X[1]}w$. Substitute Step 5 to obtain
$$\chi_XUF(w)\eta_Z=\chi_X\eta_{X[1]}w=\eta_X[1]w.$$
These are exactly the three squares in a morphism of triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The construction and the cited K-flat results use no flatness of $S$, cohomological bounds, constructibility or points.
